name: globe-translucency-bahamas
landmark: Translucent globe revealing seafloor over the Bahamas
perspective: ocean translucency demonstration over coral reefs
description: Enable Globe translucency on water bodies so the ocean surface becomes partially transparent, revealing the seafloor. Frame over the Bahamas, a region with distinctive bright turquoise shallows and dark deep-water channels, so the contrast is visible in the screenshot.
prompt: Use a public satellite imagery base layer that shows Bahamas reef and shallow-bank color contrast, such as ArcGIS World Imagery via ArcGisMapServerImageryProvider, rather than OpenStreetMap labels. Configure globe translucency without showing the opposite side of Earth through the globe: `viewer.scene.globe.translucency.enabled = true; viewer.scene.globe.translucency.frontFaceAlphaByDistance = new Cesium.NearFarScalar(400000, 0.85, 4000000, 1.0); viewer.scene.globe.translucency.backFaceAlphaByDistance = new Cesium.NearFarScalar(400000, 0.0, 4000000, 0.0);`. Set `viewer.scene.globe.undergroundColor = Cesium.Color.BLACK.withAlpha(0.0)` to clear underground colour, and `viewer.scene.skyAtmosphere.show = true`. Frame closer over the Bahamas banks: viewer.camera.setView({ destination: Cesium.Cartesian3.fromDegrees(-77.8, 24.4, 300000), orientation: { heading: 0, pitch: Cesium.Math.toRadians(-85), roll: 0 } }) or an equivalent view where turquoise banks and dark channels fill the frame.
expected_behaviors: Configures frontFaceAlphaByDistance (or front face alpha) with NearFarScalar or numeric
Uses public satellite imagery with visible Bahamas shallow-bank contrast, not only OSM labels
Frames over the Bahamas (around 24.4 N, -77.8 W) close enough for turquoise banks and dark channels to fill the screenshot
Camera is close and steeply downward enough that the Bahamas banks, not the globe back face, fill the screenshot
visual_expectations: A regional satellite view of the Bahamas with the iconic bright turquoise shallows of the Great Bahama Bank clearly visible and lighter than the surrounding deep-water dark zones. The screenshot should read as an ocean/seafloor translucency demo, not as a far-away labeled map of North America. The visual assessment uses a four-shot cardinal panorama (north, east, south, west) from the settled viewer state; the subject should remain understandable across the panorama, and grading considers all screenshots together.
